summary: Two actionable core composition gaps remain: scope reentry reuses out-of-scope historical rows as change/retirement baselines, and all-root failure bypasses failed-root uncertainty reconciliation. The new alias/interval delta and schema rebuild otherwise match their inspected test oracles. Static review only; candidate acceptance remains with the coordinator.

findings.claim: Scope reentry treats an outOfScope historical row as an active predecessor despite its closed bindings. O1 watches /watch with X at A=3; O2 watches /other and scopes X out; O3 returns to /watch. If A now contains Y=7, readPriorFileAtPath falls back to historical X, producing incoming +7 replace and retired-X -3 replace (net +4), marking X deleted. If X returns at A=8, oldObject comparison instead emits +5 modify. Both bypass scope-entry accounting across the unobserved scope boundary.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish retained out-of-scope history from an in-scope comparison baseline in both present and missing passes. Add same-identity and replacement return-to-scope regressions for both ingestion paths; establish scope-entry state without inventing growth/retirement from stale out-of-scope rows. Handle an occupied historical path without restoring a conflicting current row.

findings.claim: When every configured root fails, scanSlice returns abandoned rather than a failed-coverage observation. recordScanSlice removes transient inputs and returns before reconcileObjects. After a successful baseline, making the sole root unavailable therefore leaves its current row present and actionable and writes no observation coverage gap; mixed-root failure instead retains that row as unknown/nonactionable. Actionable currentFiles queries do not consult the abandoned generation.
findings.recommendation: Persist all-root failure uncertainty atomically without inferring deletion or replacement: retain prior identity/bytes/sample provenance, make affected current rows unknown/nonactionable, and record truthful failed coverage. Keep genuine scope-abandon behavior separate. Add sole-root and multi-root-all-failed regressions, including reopen/recovery and no lifecycle debit.
